chunks: Reward of Deeds: From his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (from his father), peace be upon them, who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) said: Whoever prays the dawn prayer and then recites 'Qul Huwa Allah Ahad' eleven times, no sin will follow him on that day, though the Devil's nose be soiled.

key_terms.رَغِمَ أَنْفَ الشَّيْطَانِ: Though the Devil's nose be soiled (humiliated)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Recite: He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas eleven times after Fajr prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from the Mu'tazila-influenced scholar Ali ibn Ja'far al-Sadiq highlights the protective efficacy of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas eleven times after Fajr, a practice often linked to the concept of 'Kaffarah' (expiation) for minor sins. The promise that 'no sin will follow' is interpreted by Shia scholars as either the prevention of new sins or the expiation of those committed, thereby humiliating the Devil who seeks to accumulate charges against the believer. This specific number (11) is sometimes correlated with the 11 gates of Hell or the 11 parts of the soul, emphasizing comprehensive spiritual cleansing.

en.ammaar-muslim: [12/1561] Thawab al-A’mal: From his father from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar from al-Amraki b. Ali from Ali b. Ja’far from his brother Musa b. Ja’far عليهما السلام who said:

Ali عليه السلام said: Whoever prays Ṣalāt al-Fajr (the dawn prayer) and then recites Qul Huwa l-Llāhu Aḥad eleven times - no sin will follow this on that day, though the Devil’s nose be soiled (i.e. though the Devil be humiliated because he will try to persuade one to sin but will not succeed however much he tries)
